[USER] The user struggles with nerves when speaking in public.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided 10 effective tips to improve public speaking skills:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Practice: The more you practice, the more confident and comfortable you will be when speaking in front of an audience.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Know your audience: Understanding the demographics and interests of your audience can help you tailor your speech to effectively communicate your message.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Be organized: Create an outline or script for your speech, including a clear introduction, main points, and conclusion.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Use body language: Nonverbal communication can be just as important as the words you speak. Use gestures, facial expressions, and posture to enhance your message.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Master your tone: Vary your tone, pitch, and volume to keep your audience interested and engaged.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Use storytelling: Telling personal stories or anecdotes can help you connect with your audience and make your message more relatable.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Take breaks: Include pauses in your speech to allow your audience to absorb what you're saying and give yourself a chance to catch your breath.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Get feedback: Record your speeches or practice in front of a trusted friend or colleague. Use their feedback to improve your speaking skills.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Focus on your message: Stay focused on your message and avoid getting sidetracked by distractions or audience reactions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. Stay positive: Believe in yourself and your ability to deliver a great speech. A positive attitude can go a long way in helping you feel confident and prepared.  
[USER] The user requested suggestions on how to calm nerves before a speech.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided suggestions to calm nerves before speaking in public:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Prepare thoroughly: Knowing your material inside and out can help you feel more confident and less nervous.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Practice deep breathing: Taking deep breaths before your speech can help relax your body and calm your nerves.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Visualize success: Imagine yourself delivering a successful speech and receiving positive feedback from your audience.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Start small: Begin by speaking in front of smaller groups or practicing your speech in front of friends and family.
